2739.fixed_record: The Council adopted Japanese–US draft S/2024/500 as resolution 2739 (2024), 12–0–3. Algeria, China and Russia abstained. It extended the Secretary-General’s reporting request under paragraph 10 of resolution 2722 (2024) through 15 January 2025, without granting new authority for military action. Japan and the United States wanted accurate, timely information about the attacks for Council deliberations. Algeria valued monthly reporting on attacks on merchant and commercial vessels to keep the Council informed. It abstained over implementation of resolution 2722 and alleged misuse or misinterpretation of self-defence through attacks on sovereign territory.
2739.candidate: Japan, the United States and Algeria valued continued reporting as a way to inform the Council about the attacks, although Algeria abstained on the resolution.

2664.fixed_record: On 9 December 2022 the Council adopted resolution 2664 by 14 votes to zero, with India abstaining. The Council kept its asset freezes in place while allowing eligible providers to meet basic human needs and deliver timely humanitarian assistance. At adoption the ISIL and Al-Qaida regime's exemption applied for two years, with the Council intending to decide on an extension. The Council requested provider due diligence to limit prohibited benefits and gave the 1267 Committee a monitoring role. India raised diversion risks, sought proactive involvement of the 1267 Monitoring Team and robust reporting, and judged those concerns not fully addressed.
2664.candidate: The Council assigned monitoring to the 1267 Committee, while India judged that its call for proactive Monitoring Team involvement and robust reporting was not fully addressed.
